name: Intro push into live word-synced captions
looks: On black, a small 'Introducing' label sits above a phone mockup showing a video editor, which the camera pushes toward. A headline lands in two colours. It cuts to the full-bleed source footage: a speaker talking, with a caption line beneath her where each word highlights in a bright box exactly as she says it.
build: The push-in is a scale/translate on the phone frame, power2.in. The headline uses list-stack-reveal's two-line landing with the second line in the accent colour. The captions use karaoke-caption-sync: each word's highlight box scales in exactly at its spoken start time, word by word, no separate line easing.
sound: A soft whoosh on the push-in, a tick on the headline's second line, then the real speech audio with a light tick per captioned word.
prompt: Introduce a transcription or captioning product by cutting straight from a title card into real talking footage, where the spoken words are captioned live, each word highlighting in a bright box exactly as it is said, so the product's core trick is the first thing proven.
